tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: Both functions give an answer, not None.

tests.name: test_script
tests.description: For the widths 64, 256 and 1,024 and the rates 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001, every width has a rate, but no one rate suits all three.
tests.message: The two functions give (False, True), not (True, False): 64 trains well at 0.1, 256 at 0.01 and 1,024 at 0.001, and each rate fails some width.

tests.name: test_one_rate_suits_all
tests.description: When one rate trains every width well, both are True.

tests.name: test_width_with_no_rate
tests.description: When some width has no rate that trains it well, both are False.

tests.name: test_rate_that_suits_no_width
tests.description: A rate that trains no width well does not stop every width from having a rate.
tests.message: For widths [64, 256] and rates [0.1, 0.01, 0.0001], every_width_has_a_rate gives False, but 64 trains well at 0.1 and 256 at 0.01. The rate 0.0001 suits neither, and the question does not ask about every rate.

tests.name: test_one_width
tests.description: one_rate_for_all: with only one width, a rate that suits that width suits all of them.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: leaked, unseen and distinct all give an answer, not None.

tests.name: test_leaked
tests.description: leaked gives the set of ids that are in both sets, and no others.

tests.name: test_unseen
tests.description: unseen gives the set of test ids that are not in the training set.

tests.name: test_distinct
tests.description: distinct counts each different id once, even when it is in both sets.
tests.message: With training ids {1, 2, 3} and test ids {3, 4}, distinct gives 5, not 4.

tests.name: test_large
tests.description: With the even ids below 10,000 for training and the multiples of 3 for testing, all three are right.
tests.message: distinct gives 8,334, but 5,000 even ids and 3,334 multiples of 3, with 1,667 in both, make 6,667 different ids.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: converse, contrapositive and short_filter are all filled in.

tests.name: test_converse
tests.description: converse is a row of the truth table where p => q and q => p differ.

tests.name: test_contrapositive
tests.description: contrapositive is False: p => q and its contrapositive agree in every row.
tests.message: contrapositive is a row of the truth table, not False. p => q and its contrapositive agree in every row, so a search for a row where they differ finds none and gives False: check what the search is asked to find, and what p => q is compared with.

tests.name: test_short_filter
tests.description: short_filter keeps exactly the emails the filter keeps, in every row of the truth table.

tests.name: test_short_filter_simplest
tests.description: short_filter is as simple as simplify_logic can make it.
